evidence_i_missed: Nothing in the other two round-1 reviews is new evidence on the merits. All three seats used the same carried extracts of the minutes and the bylaw, so our agreement on what they say is not independent retrieval.

I missed one point on how much the vote count can bear. The time-limit motion under item 1.4 drew 6 votes in favour. That meets two-thirds of all members for any committee of up to 9 members, so the special-resolution finding does not depend on taking the committee's membership as exactly the six people in the minutes' header. Later votes on the same day had only 4 or 5 voters: the additional-speaker motion under item 2.3 carried 4 to 0 without A. Knack or A. Paquette, and the 7.6 motions to go into private and back into public each carried 5 to 0. So attendance changed during the day, but the time-limit vote had all six present.

claims.proposition_evaluated: At its meeting of 2026-08-26, the Infrastructure Committee carried a motion reducing the time each approved public speaker could speak from the five minutes the Council Procedures Bylaw provides to a maximum of three minutes for that meeting, at a meeting for which about seventy people, between 60 and 80 entries on the committee's list, had been approved to speak on the bike-lane item (item 7.6).
claims.interpretation_notes: Verdict unchanged from round 1. All three seats agree on the elements that decide the verdict: a 5-minute standing limit (s.38(1)), a carried 6–0 motion under item 1.4 setting a 3-minute maximum for each approved speaker at the meeting, and N = 64 entries on item 7.6, which is inside 60–80. I recounted the carried text entry by entry. N = 15+15+15+15+4 = 64, with 15 entries carrying an organization (2+8+3+2+0). N-all = 5 (item 7.1) + 1 (item 7.3) + 9 (item 7.4: 8 plus 1 additional speaker) + 64 (item 7.6) = 79; a person approved on two items would appear twice. N-spoke = 16+16+18+2 = 52, with 12 entries carrying an organization (5+6+1+0). Rows, primary band 60–80: N 64 Supported; N-all 79 Supported; N-spoke 52 Partially supported, because the cut is established but 52 is below the band. Rows, alternative band 50–90: N, N-all and N-spoke are all Supported. N-spoke changes the row under the primary band, so the finding is definition-sensitive. It holds for people approved to speak on the item and not, under the primary band, for people recorded as presenting. The motion is the committee's, not Council's. It applied to 'each approved speaker' at the meeting, on every item, not only item 7.6. It also cut members of Council to three minutes to ask questions and three minutes to speak to or close debate on a motion, down from 5 minutes under s.38(5) and (6). It sets a maximum; the minutes do not record how long anyone actually spoke. The minutes record no reason for the motion, and this verdict establishes nothing about why it was moved, whether the people listed were complainants or where they came from, whether three minutes was enough, or which way any speaker argued.

The consolidation's amendment list ends with Bylaw 21365, October 29, 2025, and none of the later-listed amendments (Bylaws 20868, 21303, 21365) is noted against s.38.

limitations: On 2026-10-02 I tried the live minutes page, which returned HTTP 403. The bylaw PDF downloaded, but my tool could not extract its compressed text. I relied on the carried text for both: YF-EV-0209 (6 of 32 minutes items) and YF-EV-0251 (the whole bylaw). Neither was read directly from the City's site.

The carried minutes include items 1.4, 2.3, 2.4 and 7.6 in full and show no correction to items 1.4, 2.3 or 7.6. I could not check the live page for a later correction or for the minutes' approval status.
All counts are counts of entries. Because every withheld name has the same label, I cannot count distinct people or find which approved entries did not present.

Qualification 7: in the carried items, the minutes record no motion extending any speaker's time and no speaker given more or less than the limit. They record no individual speaking times. Item 7.6 in the minutes lists 5 public-speaker attachments (titles not reproduced); the carried agenda lists 10 attachments for item 7.6, none from a public speaker.

Qualification 8: no City record stating a reason for the motion was identified. I searched the carried minutes and agenda text and ran one web search on 2026-10-02 for Edmonton section 38 three-minute motions in 2026.

Qualification 9: no earlier meeting since 2025-10-29 with a motion adjusting s.38 was identified. The search was limited to that one web search, and the portal returned 403, so I could not survey earlier minutes. This absence is bounded and does not show that no such motion exists.

The CBC/Yahoo report (https://ca.news.yahoo.com/edmonton-bike-lane-expansion-continue-231838925.html), re-read on 2026-10-02, gives no count and does not mention time limits. It is not used as evidence. The search also returned a yegfacts GitHub pull request about this brief, which I did not use as a source.

claims.suggested_one_line: Yes: the Infrastructure Committee voted 6–0 to cut every approved speaker from five minutes to three for its August 26, 2026 meeting, and 64 entries were approved to speak on the bike-lane item; 52 are recorded as presenting.
claims.suggested_short_answer: Supported. The Council Procedures Bylaw gives each approved speaker five minutes (s.38(1)). At the start of its August 26, 2026 meeting, the Infrastructure Committee (not Council) carried 6–0 a motion by Councillor M. Janz setting a three-minute maximum for every approved speaker that day, and three-minute limits for councillors too. The committee's list for the bike-lane item had 64 entries in five panels, inside the 'about seventy' band; the minutes record 52 entries as presenting, which is below that band. The counts are of entries on the list, not distinct people. The minutes do not say why the motion was moved or which way any speaker argued.
suggested_tldr: The standing limit was 5 minutes per approved speaker (Bylaw 18155, s.38(1)).
Item 1.4: M. Janz moved a 3-minute maximum for every approved speaker at the meeting; carried 6–0, which meets the two-thirds special-resolution threshold.
Item 7.6 approved list: 64 entries (15, 15, 15, 15, 4), 15 with an organization's name; whole meeting: 79 entries.
Item 7.6 presentations: 52 entries (16, 16, 18, 2), below the 60–80 band, so the finding is definition-sensitive.
The minutes record no reason for the motion and no speaker's position.
